channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fails to Secure Seat on ICAO Council After Election
item.description: Kazakhstan did not secure a seat on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Council in its first attempt, finishing fifth among six candidates with 78 out of 158 votes. The election took place in Montreal during the 43rd ICAO Assembly session. Kazakhstan fell short by 32 votes to secure one of the four additional seats.

item.title: Afghanistan Faces Chronic Leadership Crisis Amidst Political Failures and Lack of Vision
item.description: Afghanistan's political history is marked by a persistent leadership crisis, lacking figures with deep political understanding and foresight. The recent speech by Taliban Supreme Leader Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada at Kabul University offered no clear message or plan to address the nation's poverty, unemployment, and despair, highlighting the ongoing absence of leaders prioritizing national interests.

item.title: Taliban Announce 481 People, Including 92 Families, Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban reported that 92 families, totaling 481 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan through various border crossings. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that significant numbers entered via Torkham and Silk Bridge, with others returning through Spin Boldak and Islam Qala.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister to Attend ECO Summit in Tehran
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's acting foreign minister, will attend the 18th Summit of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in Tehran on December 3-4. The summit will focus on regional economic cooperation, trade, and transit. Notably, the Taliban was not invited to the previous ECO summit in Islamabad.

item.title: Bishkek Wastewater Treatment Plant Undergoing Major Renovation and Modernization
item.description: Bishkek's wastewater treatment plant is being renovated across 50 hectares. The project, a public-private partnership, includes replacing equipment, implementing automated control, and energy-efficient solutions. Plans also involve installing solar panels and an odor control system. The facility, built in 1976-1980, serves Bishkek and nearby areas.

item.title: Iran Parliament Deputy Speaker Accuses Trump of Fabricating Drone Figures
item.description: Iran's Parliament Deputy Speaker Hamidreza Haji-Babaei claims US President Trump is fabricating drone figures to hide US military casualties. He stated that countries losing in competition often resort to fake statistics. Haji-Babaei asserted Iran had captured enemy drones and acquired advanced underwater military equipment.

item.title: US Senator Calls for Oversight on AI Use in War Against Iran
item.description: US Senator Kirsten Gillibrand has warned about the risks of using artificial intelligence in the war against Iran without human oversight. She called for an investigation, stating that AI is effective in intercepting missiles but lack of human control could endanger civilians, citing a school attack.

item.title: US Could Face Bankruptcy if Debt Ceiling Issue Not Resolved, Warns Trump
item.description: President Donald Trump stated that the United States could face a financial crisis and bankruptcy if the debt ceiling issue is not resolved. He proposed completely removing the statutory debt limit, citing concerns about its use as a political tool.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Local Council Powers in Budget Allocation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a decree to expand the powers of local councils. From 2028, 3-5% of local budgets will be allocated based on deputies' initiatives, allowing them to address local needs. The Ministry of Economy and Finance must draft necessary legislative changes within a month.

item.title: Afghanistan to Participate in Tehran ECO Summit After Islamabad Exclusion
item.description: Afghanistan will attend the upcoming 18th Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) summit in Tehran, led by Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi. This follows Afghanistan's exclusion from a previous ECO meeting in Islamabad, hosted by Pakistan, which cited non-recognition of the current Afghan administration.

item.title: Kyrgyz Security Council Secretary Attends Emergency Ministry Events in Tash-Komur
item.description: Adilet Orozbekov, Secretary of the Security Council of Kyrgyzstan, participated in events organized by the Ministry of Emergency Situations in Tash-Komur city, Jalal-Abad region. He attended the opening of a renovated building and a new sports ground for a rescue squad and witnessed a military oath ceremony for young soldiers. Orozbekov emphasized the ministry's growing demands due to climate change and natural disasters, noting state support for strengthening its infrastructure.

item.title: Full Video of AZAL Plane Crash Released; 2024 Incident in Kazakhstan Killed 38
item.description: The full video of the AZAL plane crash has been released. The 2024 incident in Kazakhstan resulted in 38 fatalities. A 2026 statement indicated the aircraft crashed due to an unintentional action by Russia's defense system. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: US Ambassador: NVIDIA Projects in Kazakhstan to Continue After Huang's Departure
item.description: The US Ambassador to Kazakhstan has stated that NVIDIA's projects in the country will proceed as planned, even after the departure of Jensen Huang. This assurance indicates continued investment and collaboration between NVIDIA and Kazakhstan, despite potential leadership changes within the company. The ambassador's remarks aim to reassure stakeholders about the stability and future of these technological initiatives.

item.title: Iran's Exports to Afghanistan via Dogharoun Increase by 32 Percent
item.description: Iran's exports to Afghanistan through the Dogharoun border crossing rose by 32 percent in the first seven months of the current solar year. The value of direct exports reached approximately $247.59 million. Additionally, transit shipments to Afghanistan through Dogharoun amounted to about $2.398 billion. Imports from Afghanistan also saw a significant increase, tripling in volume compared to the same period last year.

item.title: Over 12,000 Chinese-affiliated companies registered in Kazakhstan, experts warn of risks
item.description: Kazakhstan has registered over 12,000 companies with Chinese participation, with over 10,500 currently active. Experts anticipate growing Chinese business interest but caution against potential risks such as increased competition and displacement of local entrepreneurs. The true economic contribution of these companies is under scrutiny.

item.title: Three Drug Couriers Apprehended by Police in Various Regions of Kazakhstan
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan have arrested three drug couriers in different regions. In Almaty, a 56-year-old man was found with over 220 grams of ketamine. In Shymkent, a 21-year-old was detained with approximately 500 grams of synthetic drugs. A 32-year-old woman in Pavlodar was found with nearly 1.5 kg of a-PVP and 30 grams of mephedrone.

item.title: Three Afghan Migrants, Including Woman and Child, Reportedly Shot Dead by Iranian Forces
item.description: Iranian border forces allegedly shot and killed three Afghan migrants, including a woman and a child, in Sistan and Baluchestan province. A human rights organization claims security personnel concealed the bodies under rocks. Videos appear to show the victims covered with stones after being ambushed and shot.

item.title: EBRD Approves €15 Million Solar Power Plant Project in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has approved a €15 million project to build a 20 MW solar power plant in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region. The 'Chakan Solar Power Plant' will be constructed for state-owned OJSC 'Chakan GES' and includes a 6 MWh battery storage system.

item.title: Turkey Has Not Decided to Deploy Troops to Yemen, Says Foreign Minister
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that Turkey has not made a decision to deploy forces to Yemen, although it will defend Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Pact. He emphasized that defense under the pact is not automatic and requires parliamentary authorization. The pact has raised regional concerns.

item.title: Russian Military-Linked Cargo Ship Burns After Drone Strike in Gulf of Finland
item.description: A Russian cargo ship, Sparta II, linked to the military, caught fire after being struck by two drones in the Gulf of Finland. Finnish authorities believe Ukraine was likely responsible. The crew was evacuated, and Finland and Estonia are coordinating firefighting and pollution control efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adjusts Electricity Tariffs for Non-Gasified Homes in Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan will recalculate November electricity payments for homes without gas supply. Residents in non-gasified areas will be charged based on a 350 kWh basic norm instead of 200 kWh. This adjustment aims to reduce electricity expenses during the heating season, with billing system updates expected by November 25.

item.title: Bishkek Completes Reconstruction of Gogol Street
item.description: Bishkek has fully completed the reconstruction of Gogol Street, spanning approximately 1.5 kilometers from Moskovskaya to Zhumabek Street. The project included asphalting, widening the roadway, and creating parking spaces. Landscaping and infrastructure upgrades were also carried out.

item.title: Kazakhstan currency exchange rates for the weekend of November 22
item.description: Exchange rates for foreign currencies in major Kazakh cities on November 22 were as follows: US dollar sold between 455-459 tenge. In Astana, the dollar was bought at 452 and sold at 459 tenge. Euro rates were 495-505 tenge, and Russian rubles were 5.25-5.45 tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzaltyn reports significant achievements over the past five years
item.description: JSC Kyrgyzaltyn has transformed into a diversified state holding, reporting over 90 billion soms in net profit over the last five years. Its operations now span mining, logistics, construction, tourism, and investment projects, encompassing 13 subsidiaries and 5 joint ventures.

item.title: Over 200 kg of Drugs Seized in Kazakhstan; Woman Traveled from Almaty to Distribute
item.description: Kazakhstan seized over 200 kg of drugs, including marijuana, synthetics, and hashish, in the first ten days of November. Police arrested a woman in Pavlodar who had traveled from Almaty to distribute drugs, along with other suspects in various regions.

item.title: Turkey Defends Defence Pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Citing NATO Role
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan defended a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, referencing Turkey's NATO membership and past military deployment in Afghanistan. He criticized perceived double standards in the reaction to the pact.

item.title: Astana to Host World Anti-Doping Agency Executive Meetings for First Time in Central Asia
item.description: Astana will become the first city in Central Asia to host meetings of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) from November 22-27. Key WADA bodies, including the Governing Board and Executive Committee, will convene to discuss the World Anti-Doping Code and international cooperation. This marks a significant event for the region's sports governance.

item.title: GPS Tracker Fitted to Rare Lynx in Almaty Region for Scientific Study
item.description: A rare Turkestan lynx, listed in the Red Book, has been fitted with a GPS collar for the first time in Kazakhstan's Almaty region. Named Karasha, the predator will now be monitored via satellite, allowing scientists to study its life in its natural habitat.

item.title: Stigma and Misconceptions Prevent Afghans from Seeking Mental Health Treatment
item.description: Specialists in Afghanistan report that stigma, fear of being labeled "crazy," and misconceptions about psychiatric medication prevent many individuals from seeking or continuing mental health treatment. Families sometimes attribute problems to weak faith or witchcraft, opting for religious healers over doctors, which can worsen conditions.

item.title: Drought and Conflict Push Haiti Towards Widespread Famine, UN Warns
item.description: Approximately 6 million people in Haiti face food insecurity, with nearly 2 million experiencing severe hunger. The UN attributes the worsening situation to armed violence, rising food prices, and drought. Without intervention, over half the population could face famine by mid-2027.

item.title: Armenian PM Announces 'Trump Route' Project for International Peace and Prosperity
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced the launch of the 'Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity' (TRIPP) project. A key component involves connecting Armenia's electricity grid with Turkey and Azerbaijan, alongside existing links to Iran and Georgia. The project also includes infrastructure for road, rail, and energy transit.

item.title: Former Uzbek Official Sought Internationally Extradited from Turkey
item.description: A former state employee, who was internationally wanted, has been returned to Uzbekistan from Turkey. The individual is accused of embezzling state funds and forging documents during their tenure as an official at the Khorezm regional Employment Assistance department.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Banking System Undergoing Changes: Increased Client Freedom and New Security Rules
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is implementing changes to its banking system, offering more client freedom in salary account selection and tightening P2P transfer security with biometric identification. Banks will be responsible for fraudulent operations. The system aims for greater client freedom and bank responsibility, with a focus on security and service quality.

item.title: Trump Warns of US Bankruptcy Risk if Debt Limit Issue Unresolved
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated that the country could face bankruptcy if the issue of the national debt ceiling is not resolved. He proposed completely removing the legal procedure for setting the debt limit, citing it as a significant risk to the economy.

item.title: Power line connecting Uzbekistan and Tajikistan restored after outage
item.description: An outage on the 500 kV "L-503" power line, connecting Uzbekistan's "Sirdaryo" thermal power station and "Uzbekistan" substation via Tajikistan, has been fully repaired. The line was restored on November 22. The incident occurred on November 19 due to adverse weather conditions and difficult terrain, causing temporary power restrictions in parts of the Fergana Valley.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to liquidate UK-sanctioned company 'Processing.kg'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has decided to liquidate OAO 'Processing.kg', a company that received 200 million soms in state capital increase. The company and its head were sanctioned by the UK a month prior. The Ministry of Finance, as the sole shareholder, approved the liquidation on November 16, 2026.

item.title: Power outage resolved after electricity pylon collapse on L-503 line
item.description: The power outage caused by the collapse of an electricity pylon on the L-503 transmission line, connecting the "Sirdaryo" thermal power plant and the "Uzbekistan" substation, has been fully resolved. Electricity transmission through the line, which passes through Tajikistan, has been restored.

item.title: Zelensky Proposes Evacuating 15 Settlements, Citing Oleshki Example
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky has proposed evacuating 15 settlements, using Oleshki as an example. The proposal includes locations in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, with the list potentially expanding based on population and conditions.

item.title: Taliban Report Three Armed Robbers Killed in Kabul
item.description: The Taliban authorities have reported that three armed robbers were killed in Kabul. Further details regarding the incident, the identities of the individuals, or the circumstances of their deaths were not provided in the source text.

item.title: New Hippodrome Construction Begins in Sokuluk, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A project to build a National Equestrian Sports Complex is underway in Sokuluk, Kyrgyzstan. The complex will feature a 10,000-seat hippodrome for races and a 25,000-seat arena for Kok Boru. The Bishkek mayor's office announced the plans, which include modern facilities and infrastructure on a 114-hectare site.
